content: The recommended dosage is 20 mg of antimony (Sb) per kilogram of body weight per day, with a maximum dose of 850 mg, administered either intravenously (IV) or intramuscularly (IM) for a duration of 20 to 28 days. This medication is available exclusively in the United States through the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) under an orphan drug designation for the treatment of acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Potential side effects include anorexia, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, changes in electrocardiogram (ECG) readings, headache, lethargy, muscle pain (myalgia), elevated liver enzymes, coughing accompanied by substernal pain, and, in rare cases, anaphylaxis. Other reported adverse effects include fever, sweating, flushing, vertigo, nosebleeds or gum bleeding, jaundice, skin rash, pain and thrombosis at the site of intravenous administration, and pain associated with intramuscular injections. Hypersensitivity reactions and significant renal impairment have also been noted. The safety of this medication during pregnancy and lactation is unknown. It is categorized as Pregnancy Category A, meaning that controlled studies in pregnant women have not shown evidence of fetal risk. However, its metabolism and excretion pathways remain unidentified. The drug is known to reduce fructose diphosphate levels and inhibit glycolysis. For formulary comparisons with other drugs in the same class, users are advised to create a list of plans, which can be saved and edited as needed. This allows for the review of formulary information, which may vary between individual plans and is subject to change. It is recommended to contact the relevant plan provider for the most up-to-date information. The information provided here is intended for general informational and educational purposes only.
